behavioral_notes.observation: Executes a single multi-CTE SQL statement directly on the database (env.cr.execute). The query handles three scenarios in one pass: (a) base lines — joins account_move_line through account_move_line_account_tax_rel, account_tax_filiation_rel (for child/group taxes), and account_tax_repartition_line to find the correct repartition line based on document_type ('invoice' or 'refund') and move_type; (b) tax lines — joins via aml.tax_repartition_line_id directly; (c) fuses both, DELETEs all existing tags from account_account_tag_account_move_line_rel for those amls, then INSERTs the current tags from account_account_tag_account_tax_repartition_line_rel. Calls env.flush_all() before and env.invalidate_all() after to keep the ORM cache consistent. Returns the array of impacted aml ids.

For 'entry' move type (general journal entries, not invoices/refunds), the SQL determines document_type by sign of balance and tax type: sale tax + balance<=0 -> 'invoice', sale tax + balance>0 -> 'refund'; purchase tax + balance>=0 -> 'invoice', purchase tax + balance<0 -> 'refund'. This logic mirrors the original tagging algorithm and is entirely within the SQL CTE — invisible from the model schema.

Before calling _modify_tag_to_aml_relation, searches for account.tax records with children_tax_ids set (group taxes). Collects all child tax ids and raises UserError if any child tax appears under more than one parent (len(children_taxes) > len(parent_taxes.children_tax_ids.ids)), because the SQL join through account_tax_filiation_rel would produce duplicate rows in that case. This is an explicit unsupported-scenario guard.

date_from defaults to company.tax_lock_date + 1 day if a tax lock date exists, otherwise to context_today. The display_lock_date_warning Boolean fires if the user manually sets date_from to a date before company.tax_lock_date — shown as a warning banner in the wizard form but does not block execution, making this a non-enforced advisory.

The wizard is surfaced inside res.config.settings under the 'default_taxes_setting_container' block, gated to groups='base.group_no_one' (technical/developer mode only). This means the feature is intentionally hidden from regular accounting users — it is an expert/admin tool exposed only in developer mode, not via a menu item.

data_objects: account.tax.repartition.line (source of truth for new tags)
information_flows: side-effect: wizard.update_amls_tax_tags -> raw SQL DELETE+INSERT on account_account_tag_account_move_line_rel for all in-scope amls
scope: company_id + date_from filter; CABA (cash basis) moves resolved via tax_cash_basis_origin_move_id join

capabilities: Retroactively synchronise tax grid tags on existing journal items to match the current tax repartition line configuration
Scope the update by company and start date (does not touch history before date_from)
Handle group/child taxes (account_tax_filiation_rel) and cash-basis moves (CABA)
Advisory warning when date_from precedes the company tax lock date
value_streams: Tax-Configuration-Correction: admin changes tax repartition lines (adds/changes grid tags) -> runs wizard -> historical amls retroactively re-tagged -> tax grid reports now consistent
information_concepts: account.move.line (journal item whose tax_tag_ids are updated)
account.account.tag (tax grid tag / account.account.tag with applicability='taxes')
organization: base.group_no_one (developer/technical mode — wizard only visible in Settings when developer mode is active)
policies: Update is scoped to a single company (company_id, readonly in wizard)
Update only affects amls with date >= date_from
Child taxes belonging to multiple parent group taxes are explicitly unsupported (UserError raised)
The operation is irreversible — the wizard form warns 'highly recommended to backup your database beforehand'
The wizard does NOT enforce the tax lock date; it only shows a warning banner if date_from < tax_lock_date
Updates apply regardless of the journal entry state (posted, draft, or cancelled)
stakeholders: System Administrator / Technical Accountant (configures taxes and runs the retroactive fix)
Auditor (relies on consistent tax grid tags for fiscal reporting)

classification.rationale: account_update_tax_tags is a data-integrity maintenance tool for the accounting subsystem: it corrects tax grid tag assignments on historical journal items after a tax configuration change. It creates no business object and performs no revenue-generating or operational activity. It is pure firm infrastructure (Stabell & Fjeldstad support), enabling accurate fiscal reporting (APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources) after a tax configuration change.

standard_capabilities: One-shot retroactive re-tagging of all account.move.line tax grids from a specified date
Cash-basis (CABA) move handling via tax_cash_basis_origin_move_id join
Accessible only in developer mode (base.group_no_one) from Accounting Settings
typical_fits: After a country localization upgrade changes tax repartition lines and grid tags
After a company reconfigures taxes mid-year and needs historical reports to reflect the new tags
One-time data repair after an import/migration that created amls with stale or missing tax tags
common_gaps: No preview/dry-run mode — the operation directly mutates the database
No rollback mechanism — the wizard form advises a backup but provides no undo
Child tax belonging to multiple parents is unsupported and raises a hard UserError
No granularity below the date_from cutoff (cannot target a subset of taxes or journals)
The tax lock date is advisory only — the wizard will overwrite locked-period entries if the user proceeds
drive_hints: Settings -> Technical (developer mode) -> Accounting -> Tax section -> 'Update tax tags on existing Journal Entries'

open_questions: Does the SQL CTE correctly handle amls with multiple taxes on the same line when one tax is a group and another is a standalone tax simultaneously?
Does the wizard need to be re-run after each l10n tax grid update, or is there a hook that triggers it automatically?
What is the performance profile for large databases (millions of amls)? The single-CTE approach has no chunking.
